description: **August 6, 1945**, an atomic bomb leveled Hiroshima. Three days later, Nagasaki. World War II ends…and the nuclear age begins.

hero.hook: In a flash brighter than a thousand suns, an entire city disappears.

blocks.text: On **August 6, 1945**, at **8:15 a.m.**, the sky of **Hiroshima**, a Japanese city, burst into flames. In an instant, a single bomb kills between **70,000 and 80,000** people. Three days later, **Nagasaki** suffered the same fate.
These strikes end the war in Asia and open the **nuclear era**: for the first time, humanity has a weapon capable of self-destruction.

For fear of a Nazi bomb, a letter from Albert Einstein, written with the physicist , pushes Washington to act. In **1942**, the United States launched the **Manhattan Project**: approximately **130,000** people, **2 billion** dollars. Secret sites are born at Oak Ridge, Hanford, Los Alamos. [[Leó Szilárd]]

blocks.caption: The Trinity test, July 16, 1945: the first nuclear explosion.

blocks.text: The **Trinity** test, in the desert of  (New Mexico), was so powerful that residents more than **150 km** thought they saw the sun rise twice. [[Jornada del Muerto]]

On **July 16, 1945**, the **Trinity** test passed. **Robert Oppenheimer**, scientific director of the project, then thinks of a sentence from the Mahabharata, an ancient Indian text: “I have become Death, the destroyer of worlds. »

When Franklin Roosevelt died, the new American president **Harry Truman** discovered the existence of the bomb. Germany has capitulated, but Japan continues, notably with the [[Kamikazes]], pilots who rush their planes against Allied ships. An invasion of Japan could cost **500, 000 to a million** in American losses.
Hiroshima had been deliberately spared from conventional raids, to precisely measure the effects of a single nuclear explosion.

At , an Allied conference in July 1945, tensions with the USSR rose. Using the bomb is also a display of American power. Hiroshima was chosen for its military role and its basin-shaped relief, which concentrates the breath. [[Potsdam]]

On **August 6**, the bomber **Enola Gay** drops **Little Boy** on Hiroshima. Up to **140,000** dead by the end of the year, including burns and . On **August 9**,  first aims for , but the clouds send it back to **Nagasaki**. The **Fat Man** bomb explodes. [[Radiation sickness (acute radiation syndrome)]] [[Bockscar]] [[Kokura]]

blocks.caption: The mushroom cloud of Hiroshima, August 6, 1945.

blocks.text: **Tsutomu Yamaguchi** survived both bombs: injured in Hiroshima on the 6th, he returned to Nagasaki... where he was still on August 9.

The same day, the [[USSR enters the war against Japan (August 9, 1945)]] destroyed the hope of Soviet mediation. On **August 15**, Emperor **Hirohito** announces the surrender on the radio, in, a historic speech. [[Gyokuon-hōsō]]

The survivors, the [[Hibakusha]], carry cancers, stigmas and an endless ethical debate. Geopolitically, the age of begins: threatening to use the bomb to prevent the other from attacking. The Cold War begins. Hiroshima remains the harshest warning of science put at the service of destruction. [[Nuclear deterrence]]
